text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Romanian Premier Victor Ciorbea and Hungarian Premier Gyula Horn and politicians in their entourage signed five agreements on the first day of the Romanian leader's visit. Ciorbea told Horn that a minority law will soon be passed, the education law will be amended, the posting of bilingual signs will be guaranteed and the use of the native language in all walks of public administration will be ensured.
- The board of directors of the World Bank yesterday approved a 12-year, $225 million loan package for Hungary, to be used to upgrade the banking sector.

- The number of farmers demonstrating against the new tax and social insurance regulations continued to drop on Wednesday. Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy will present the national agrarian programme in Godollo today.
- A Strasbourg meeting of rival Christian Democrat factions organised by EUCD President Wim van Velzen for this weekend has fallen through because party president Gyorgy Giczy has a busy schedule.
- The Economic Competition Office yesterday fined the car maker Suzuki Rt. HUF 30 million for fixing the retail price of cars.
- Experts from the Economic Competition Office declared yesterday that the privatisation of the Hungarian Electricity Works is not reasonable from the point of view of competition.
- The board of directors of the State Privatisation & Holding Co. yesterday approved a proposal on the strategy for K&H Bank's privatisation.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The cabinet today is expected to discuss a report drafted by the Ministry of Transport on motorway development.
- The Hungarian Oil & Gas Co. MOL will start a several-week long road show in mid-April, promoting the issue of 20 percent of its shares.

- Public Library and Public Education Workers Union president Janos Vadasz said 6,000-7,000 of the 22,000 persons employed in public education have failed to receive salaries as specified under law and urged the labour minister to start an investigation.
- The Banking Association decided at a Wednesday meeting to investigate the reasons and consequences of the recent run on Postabank branches.

- The rate of unemployment is higher among Gypsies, the opportunities of Roma children to pursue higher studies are bad, and their influx to urban settlements goes hand-in-hand with a process of ghettoisation, says a government report.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The president of the Higher Education Union warned to form a national strike committee unless an agreement is reached on salary payment.
- Pope John Paul II yesterday received Sandor Lezsak, president of the Democratic Forum.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs arrived in Argentina Wednesday after winding up talks in Chile earlier in the day.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The state news agency MTI may become insolvent in a month if does not receive assistance, said acting managing director and financial director Gabor Tompa.
